issues.description: Race condition on is_registered flag allows concurrent requests to skip sending LoRA weights
issues.detail: In _create_trtllm_generate_request, lora_config.is_registered is checked and set without synchronization. Two concurrent first-time requests for the same LoRA can both see is_registered=False and race, or worse, one sets it True before the server has actually registered the weights, causing subsequent requests to send only the task_id while the server has no cached LoRA. This is an async FastAPI engine so concurrency is real.

issues.description: LoRA weights loaded from disk on every first request, blocking the async event loop
issues.detail: np.load() on lora_weights.npy and lora_config.npy runs synchronously inside an async request path. Large LoRA tensors will block the event loop for noticeable time, stalling all other requests. Weights should be pre-loaded at startup (in _parse_lora_configs) and cached on the TritonLoraConfig dataclass, not lazy-loaded per request.

issues.description: Variable shadowing of lora_config_path causes incorrect error reporting and confusion
issues.detail: In _parse_lora_configs, lora_config_path is set to multi_lora.json at line ~658, then reassigned inside the for-loop to model.lora_config.npy. After the loop iteration, subsequent error paths or reads referring to lora_config_path will use the wrong value. Use a distinct name like lora_config_npy_path.

issues.description: Debug print statements left in production code paths
issues.detail: print(f"backend: {backend}") inside the per-LoRA loop, and traceback.format_exc() prints added in chat.py, completions.py, embeddings.py, and triton.py will spam stdout for every request/error. These look like debugging leftovers and should be replaced with proper logging at appropriate levels, or removed.

issues.description: Return type annotation of _parse_lora_configs is wrong
issues.detail: The function signature declares return type `None | List[tuple[str, str]]` but it actually returns `None | List[TritonLoraConfig]`. This will mislead readers and any type checker. Update to `Optional[List[TritonLoraConfig]]`.

issues.description: _get_lora_config can NPE when model_name not in metadata and lora_name is provided
issues.detail: self.model_metadata.get(model_name) returns None if not found, then `model_metadata.lora_configs` raises AttributeError instead of a clean ClientError. Also the function is annotated to return TritonLoraConfig but can return None. Should guard model_metadata is not None and update return annotation to Optional[TritonLoraConfig].

review.summary: This PR adds multi-LoRA support for TensorRT-LLM in the OpenAI-compatible frontend. The most serious concerns are concurrency-safety around the `is_registered` flag (race conditions on first request can leave the server without cached weights) and synchronous `np.load` on large tensors inside the async request path. There are also code-hygiene issues: variable shadowing of `lora_config_path`, debug `print` and `traceback.format_exc()` calls scattered across routers and utils, a wrong return-type annotation, and a potential None-deref in `_get_lora_config`. Function-level behavior otherwise looks consistent with the vLLM path being preserved.
